title: Stock Market Today Live, Sept 11: Sensex, Nifty stay under pressure as Brent crude hits $108 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Candle stick graph chart of stock market investment trading, Stock exchange concept design and background. Vector illustrations. | Photo Credit: EMOJOEZ

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 11 September 2026.

Indian shares remained weak in range-bound afternoon trade on Friday as Brent crude surged to $108 a barrel amid escalating West Asia hostilities, raising concerns over inflation, India’s import bill and corporate margins.

At 1.23 p.m., the Sensex was down 383.60 points, or 0.51 per cent, at 74,518.99, while the Nifty fell 138.85 points, or 0.59 per cent, to 23,338.95.

The Nifty and Sensex have declined 1.8% and 2.1%, respectively, this week, putting both benchmarks on track for their fifth consecutive weekly fall.

Rising oil prices have also pushed global bond yields higher and pressured equities, with MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan down 1.8%.

Foreign investors sold ₹438 crore of Indian shares on Thursday and have offloaded $1.36 billion so far in September. A busy IPO season has added pressure.

* Nifty breaks key support at 23,400 — a clear bearish signal, with the index trading below this important level.

* Intraday resistance at 23,300–23,330 — the immediate upside zone is likely to cap any recovery.

* Downside risk towards 23,000 — sustained weakness below 23,400 could expose the index to the psychological 23,000 level.

* Nifty September Futures below 23,400 — the futures contract remains bearish, with 23,280 as immediate support and 23,100 as the next downside level.

* Very negative advance-decline ratio — the 10:40 ratio indicates broad-based market weakness and confirms the negative sentiment.

* Key levels: Support — 23,280, 23,100 | Resistance — 23,400, 23,450.

Alembic Pharma's Vadodara facility passes USFDA inspection with zero observations, confirming regulatory compliance and operational excellence.

IPO-bound Paramotor Digital Technology Limited has announced multiple collaborations at the Global Fintech Festival 2026, including arrangements with Mastercard Asia/Pacific Pte. Ltd. and NSDL Payments Bank Limited for the launch of new gift cards and prepaid cards.

The Company has also announced an ecosystem arrangement with TBX (formerly TransBnk) to explore opportunities across digital payments, rewards, loyalty, gifting and transaction banking infrastructure, and has partnered with Osmo Atorie LLP to provide technology and infrastructure services for its closed-loop card.

At Global Fintech Fest 2026, Xflow, a cross-border payments platform, today announced a partnership with HSBC that enables global businesses to collect payments from Indian customers using cards, net banking, and UPI for online and recurring payments. By using India’s local payment infrastructure, businesses anywhere in the world can use Xflow to offer Indian buyers a familiar, local checkout experience, without taking on additional local regulatory obligations or establishing an entity in India. The solution was unveiled at Global Fintech Fest, one of the world’s largest fintech gatherings, in Mumbai

Traditionally, collecting payments from India has been very difficult for international merchants. Fewer than 70% of international card transactions succeed in India, as many cards are not enabled for overseas spending, and recurring payments face additional friction due to India’s data and mandate requirements. Bank wire transfers can be slow, costly, and paperwork-heavy. These hurdles cause global merchants to lose Indian customers at checkout.

Xflow resolves this by turning cross-border payments into local transactions for Indian buyers. At checkout, buyers can pay through UPI and cards. These are methods they already use and trust. UPI alone accounts for roughly 85% of India’s digital payment volumes. These local methods settle quick and deliver a 95%+ success rate, driving higher conversion for global merchants.

National Stock Exchange (NSE), India’s largest stock exchange, will open its initial public ​offering next week.

The rupee was on course for a more than 1% weekly fall on ‌Friday as a sharp rise in oil prices heaped pressure on Indian markets ⁠even as central bank intervention limited the currency’s decline.

Stocks and bonds in Mumbai fell, and the ‌rupee declined 0.3% to 95.70, weakening for the fourth straight day.

“The immediate ‌support zone is now placed at ‌95.10–95.20. ⁠A sustained move above 95.50–95.80 could open ⁠the door towards 96.00–96.20 in the coming sessions,” said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex.

Brent remained above $100 per ‌barrel as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuelled fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies. - Reuters

Alembic Pharmaceuticals on Friday said the US health regulator has completed an unannounced inspection at its bioequivalence facility in Vadodara, Gujarat, with zero observation.

In a regulatory filing, the company said the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) carried out the onsite bioequivalence inspection from August 31, 2026, to September 10, 2026.

· Price Movement – Gold and silver came under selling pressure on Wednesday as traders booked profits following a stronger-than-expected US PPI print, which reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates. Attention now shifts to today’s US CPI release for further confirmation of the inflation trajectory. Adding to the hawkish undertone, the European Central Bank lifted its own borrowing costs in line with forecasts and cautioned that inflation risks still skew to the upside — a signal that pushed traders to raise their bets on additional ECB tightening ahead.

· Geopolitical tensions – Tensions in the Middle East escalated further after Iran-aligned Houthi forces took control of Yemen’s port city of Mocha, pressing their advance down the Red Sea
